directAnswer: Pope Gregory XIV was Niccolo Sfondrati, a Lombard bishop and friend of St. Charles Borromeo, who reigned from December 1590 to October 1591. His short pontificate is remembered for strong support of the Catholic League against Henry of Navarre, a bull forbidding betting on papal elections, and the softening of Sixtus V's penalties on abortion.

sections.h2: Bishop of Cremona and Friend of Borromeo
paras: Niccolo Sfondrati was born on 11 February 1535 at Somma Lombardo, near Milan, the son of a senator who later became a cardinal. He studied law, became bishop of Cremona in 1560, and took part in the final sessions of the Council of Trent.

A close friend of St. Charles Borromeo and of St. Philip Neri, he was known for personal piety and simplicity. Gregory XIII made him a cardinal in 1583. After a two-month conclave dominated by Spanish influence, he was elected on 5 December 1590.

sections.h2: The Catholic League and Henry of Navarre
paras: France was then torn by the Wars of Religion. Gregory XIV renewed the excommunication of the Protestant Henry of Navarre, heir to the French throne, and sent money and troops under his nephew Ercole Sfondrati to aid the Catholic League. The expedition achieved little.
His nephew Paolo Emilio Sfondrati, whom he made a cardinal, took over much of the administration, and the pope's frequent illness left him limited capacity to govern personally.

In 1591 Gregory XIV issued the bull Cogit nos, forbidding wagers on the outcome of papal elections, the length of a pontificate or the creation of cardinals, under pain of excommunication. Betting on conclaves had become a popular pastime among Roman bankers and merchants.

In the same year his constitution Sedes Apostolica modified the severe penalties of Sixtus V's Effraenatam, restricting the reserved excommunication for abortion to cases after the fetus was considered animated, following the medieval distinction then current, and dropping it for contraception. During his reign Rome also endured famine and plague. Gregory XIV died on 16 October 1591.

keyFacts: Born Niccolo Sfondrati at Somma Lombardo on 11 February 1535
Bishop of Cremona and participant at the Council of Trent
Friend of St. Charles Borromeo and St. Philip Neri
Supported the Catholic League against Henry of Navarre
Banned betting on papal elections with Cogit nos (1591)

faqs.question: Why did Gregory XIV ban betting on papal elections?
faqs.answer: Wagering on conclaves and the creation of cardinals had become common in Rome. His 1591 bull Cogit nos made such bets punishable by excommunication to protect the dignity of the election.

faqs.question: How did Gregory XIV change Sixtus V's law on abortion?
faqs.answer: His 1591 constitution Sedes Apostolica limited the special excommunication to abortion of an ensouled fetus, as theologians of the time understood it, and removed it for contraception. The Church's moral teaching that abortion is gravely wrong was not changed.
